scope: June 24/29 1917 JACAR 0509/0511; limited public-source audit of additional June–September traffic, Dai report and named codebooks

records.title: Sun Yat-sen ↔ Dai Jitao, Shanghai–Tokyo, March 1917 — NOTES.md
records.access_method: GitHub web page plus GitHub connector full source
directly_verified: Author source labels June 0509/0511 as unread and a different system from March.
Author inventories B03050090200 as 0503–0513, 11 images, administrative dates 1917-03-29 to 1917-09-21.
Author identifies 0508 and 0513 as clear Japanese kana telegrams; 0513 is dated 1917-09-09.
records.relationship_to_june: Direct modern research on the targets; inventory information is an author's report, not this audit's direct inspection of all original frames.
records.evidence_grade: R: directly read author research; not archival image verification
records.novelty: Existing source rechecked; no new June decipherment; explicit scope guard for September telegram
records.next_step: Obtain official item images and verify the non-June frames before expanding the same-key corpus.
failures_or_access_limits: Author notes are not the official images.

records.title: 电报逐封细读 — author HTML source, y1917-tpl
records.access_method: GitHub connector full HTML source, including template content
directly_verified: The June template explicitly marks both targets unsolved.
The current introduction refers to 26 newly deciphered telegrams from April–June 1916, not June 1917.
The author still presents inversion/transposition of irregular pairs as an interpretation, not deletion as established historical fact.
records.relationship_to_june: Independent modern transcript and interpretation; no current historical key or accepted June plaintext.
records.novelty: Existing source rechecked; 26 is an updated 1916 corpus count and not target progress.
records.next_step: Keep R18 deletion as a competing hypothesis and carry the author's alternate transcript in sensitivity checks.
failures_or_access_limits: Initial web fetch returned cache miss; connector full HTML succeeded.
No claim about the author's unpublished work.

records.title: 资料来源与致谢 — author source register
directly_verified: B03050090200 is listed separately from the newly deciphered 1916 items.

records.relationship_to_june: Useful for avoiding false chronological inclusion; these cited earlier items are not proven same-key June 1917 traffic.
records.evidence_grade: R: author source register, original archive contents not newly inspected
records.novelty: Existing references rechecked, not new raw archival data.
records.next_step: Search other 1917 holdings by date and correspondents, not just adjacent numeric archive codes.
failures_or_access_limits: No fifth-volume reference code located or verified.

records.title: U. Kuzuoglu (2018), Chinese cryptography: The Chinese Nationalist Party and intelligence management, 1927–1949
records.access_method: Author-uploaded full-text page directly opened; footnotes 4–6 and bibliography read, not just search snippets
directly_verified: Footnote 5 cites Ren mi, 1913/4, yiban050/5.3; Yong mi, 1923/9, yiban050/5.32; Dong mi, 1922/6, yiban050/5.33; Cheng mi, 1922/6, yiban050/5.35.
Bibliography cites the undated title 'Hu Hanmin yu Kong Geng wanglai suoyong tong mi dianmaben' at yiban050/5.7.
The 1918 Japanese-code explanation and table no. 64 references remain yiban050/1.2 and yiban333/2.2.
records.relationship_to_june: Evidence for named and privately used codebooks. No documented tie of any listed item to the June 1917 targets.
records.evidence_grade: B: primary scholarly archival citation; not the original codebook or current archive catalogue
records.novelty: yiban050/5.7 is a newly extracted lead relative to the inspected R14–R18 reports and handoff; other references are existing leads with clarified dates.
records.next_step: Verify title characters, date and image availability in the current catalogue. Prioritize 1913 Ren mi and date the undated Hu–Kong item before testing; 1922/1923 copies cannot themselves establish a 1917 key.
failures_or_access_limits: No codebook scan or contemporaneous cipher instruction acquired.
The Chinese characters for 'tong mi' were not verified and are deliberately not supplied.
The paper is historical evidence for holdings, not proof of today's access or target usage.
